definitions.explanation: Unwilling to change one's opinions, attitudes, or actions despite good reasons to do so. Can describe a person's character or specific behavior.
Difficult to remove or get rid of. Used for things that won't go away easily.

examples.japanese: うちの{父|ちち}は{頑固|がんこ}で、{一度|いちど}{決|き}めたら{絶対|ぜったい}に{変|か}えない。
examples.english: My father is stubborn—once he's decided something, he absolutely won't change his mind.

examples.japanese: {頑固|がんこ}な{汚|よご}れがなかなか{落|お}ちない。
examples.english: The stubborn stain won't come off easily.

examples.japanese: {頑固親父|がんこおやじ}だけど、{根|ね}は{優|やさ}しい。
examples.english: He's a stubborn old man, but he's kind at heart.

examples.japanese: {頑固|がんこ}な{風邪|かぜ}がなかなか{治|なお}らない。
examples.english: This stubborn cold just won't go away.

examples.japanese: この{油|あぶら}{汚|よご}れは{頑固|がんこ}で、{普通|ふつう}の{洗剤|せんざい}では{落|お}ちなかった。
examples.english: This grease stain is so stubborn that regular detergent couldn't get it off.

examples.japanese: {祖父|そふ}は{頑固|がんこ}に{自分|じぶん}のやり{方|かた}を{貫|つらぬ}いてきた{職人|しょくにん}だった。
examples.english: My grandfather was a craftsman who stubbornly stuck to his own methods throughout his career.

notes:
USAGE:
・{頑固|がんこ}な{人|ひと} (a stubborn person)
・{頑固|がんこ}に{反対|はんたい}する (to stubbornly oppose)
・{頑固|がんこ}を{通|とお}す (to stick stubbornly to one's position)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{頑固親父|がんこおやじ} (stubborn old man - often used affectionately)
・{頑固|がんこ}な{職人|しょくにん} (stubborn craftsman - can be positive, implying commitment to quality)
・{頑固|がんこ}な{風邪|かぜ} (stubborn cold that won't go away)
・{頑固|がんこ}な{汚|よご}れ} (stubborn stain)

NUANCE:
For people, usually negative but can be used with grudging respect for someone who sticks to their principles. {頑固親父|がんこおやじ} often carries affection despite the complaint.

RELATED WORDS:
・{強情|ごうじょう} (obstinate - more negative)
・{意地|いじ}っ{張|ぱ}り (obstinate, contrary)
